integrity: A complete 2001 manuscript using the Tinkerbell map for nonlinear time-series inference was inspected at the exact-equation and state-reconstruction sections. A complete 2011 same-object article was inspected at the map-definition, standard-parameter, shadowing, and rigorous-chaos sections; targeted full-text searches found no covariance, moment, invariant-measure, average, or mean theorem matching the accepted statement. Later q-deformed and fractional Tinkerbell work was compared at stated-scope level for possible broader coverage. The invariant raw-moment identities, covariance reduction, eigenvalue gap, centered isotropy, and classical rational specialization were reconstructed independently, and the algebra was replayed with the packaged checker.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is a necessary invariant-measure constraint and does not prove existence or uniqueness of a physical measure.
The barycenter determines the traceless covariance but not its trace.
The rank-one equality case does not classify which invariant affine lines can actually occur.
A 1996 book predates the structured date but was not assigned an invented day-level public date.
A differently phrased pseudocovariance identity could remain in unindexed literature.
title: Barycenter-determined covariance anisotropy in the Tinkerbell map
